facts.fact: The article was published on May 18, 2026.
The author recommends placing live chat most often on pages tied directly to revenue, especially service pages, quote pages, and checkout paths.
facts.quote: I recommend chat most often on pages tied directly to revenue, especially service pages, quote pages, and checkout paths.

facts.fact: The article's stated practical rule is to put live chat on high-intent pages first, especially pages tied to quote requests, bookings, and service decisions.
facts.quote: Put live chat on high-intent pages first, especially pages tied to quote requests, bookings, and service decisions.

facts.fact: The article recommends that businesses state response timing clearly in chat, saying if replies come in a few minutes, say that rather than implying instant support.
facts.quote: If replies come in a few minutes, say that instead of implying instant support.

facts.fact: The article recommends asking for service type, timeline, location, or budget range early in a chat so the conversation produces a usable lead.
facts.quote: Ask for service type, timeline, location, or budget range early so the conversation produces an usable lead.

facts.fact: The article attributes to Forrester research the finding that live chat has long been pointed to as a conversion aid; no figure is given.
facts.quote: Research from Forrester has long pointed to live chat as a conversion aid because it helps buyers get answers before hesitation turns into an exit.

facts.fact: The article cites Zendesk industry research as finding that customers often prefer live chat for fast, low-effort help during the buying process; no figure is given.
facts.quote: Industry research from Zendesk has found that customers often prefer live chat for fast, low-effort help during the buying process

facts.fact: Intercom states in its guide to live chat for customer service that chat gives businesses direct access to customer questions in real time.
facts.quote: Intercom explains in its guide to live chat for customer service that chat gives businesses direct access to customer questions in real time

facts.fact: Zendesk notes in its overview of live chat customer service that chat supports personalized, convenient interactions.
facts.quote: Zendesk notes in its overview of live chat customer service that chat supports personalized, convenient interactions

facts.fact: Adwave recommends reviewing chat transcripts every week, which it describes as frequent enough to catch patterns before wasted ad spend builds up.
facts.quote: Review transcripts every week: Weekly review is frequent enough to catch patterns before wasted ad spend piles up.

facts.fact: Adwave suggests a starting set of chat tags: pricing, availability, service area, trust concerns, urgency, and competitor comparisons.
facts.quote: Pricing, availability, service area, trust concerns, urgency, and competitor comparisons are a strong starting set.

facts.fact: Adwave states that acquiring a new customer usually costs more than keeping an existing one, without giving a specific cost figure.
facts.quote: Acquiring a new customer usually costs more than keeping an existing one.

facts.fact: Adwave describes itself as helping small businesses create, launch, and measure TV advertising campaigns that drive local viewers to their websites.
facts.quote: Adwave helps small businesses create, launch, and measure TV advertising campaigns that drive local viewers to their websites.

facts.fact: Adwave states that it helps small businesses create and launch TV ads on premium channels.
facts.quote: It helps small businesses create and launch TV ads on premium channels

facts.fact: Harvard Business Review has reported (third-party claim, no figure given) that customers whose issues are resolved quickly are more likely to remain loyal than those who face delayed service.
facts.quote: Harvard Business Review has reported that customers whose issues are resolved quickly are more likely to remain loyal than those who face delayed service
